messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: cvodes_integrator feedback?
parts:
Hi there!

It would be great if someone would take the time to have a quick look at the design of the cvodes_integrator:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/blob/feature/issue-262-CVODES-2/stan/math/rev/mat/functor/cvodes_integrator.hpp

The cvodes_integrator should now be in the state as we discussed last week in the meeting and other important bit, the ode_system, also got discussed such that I believe we are very far with this pull, I guess.

From the cvodes pull request the objects which would still require a review and tests are

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/blob/feature/issue-262-CVODES-2/stan/math/rev/mat/functor/ode_system.hpp

and

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/blob/feature/issue-262-CVODES-2/stan/math/rev/arr/fun/decouple_ode_states.hpp

The entry function

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/blob/feature/issue-262-CVODES-2/stan/math/rev/mat/functor/integrate_ode_bdf.hpp

already got reviewed.

As I have tomorrow a full day time to work on these things, I could get this in a state where it would be ready to be merged (at least I would hope so). For that to happen it would be great if you could give me some input on the testing strategy. My understanding of this would be that I use the objects in the intended way with my tests and check for correctness.

The pull request with all comments leading to the current state is in
https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/283

Thanks a lot!

Best,
Sebastian


(wishful thinking ... getting this out with 2.10 could still be an option ...)

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] cvodes_integrator feedback?
parts:
Firstly, a reminder that moving forward we should use more descriptive branch names,
at least not having mysterious numerical labels! Something like “refactor_integrate_ode”
would be appropriate here, and the branch name can be changed so don’t hesitate to
do so before a pull request.

ode_system.hpp

Line 14: No reason to have abbreviations in comments.

Line 15: “S” and “P” aren’t used in this implementation, no need to define them.

Line 21: If it’s got methods, it’s a class. Just style.

Line 57, 76, etc: Qualitifers/types on same line. So “inline void” instead of “inline\nvoid”

integrate_ode_bdf.hpp

Line 32: No abbreviations. This is worth a few sentences.

Line 87: I recommend breaking this line to


cvodes_integrator<F, T_initial, T_param>
integrator(f, y0, t0,…

to free up lots of vertical space.

cvodes_integrator.hpp

Line 44: Why is ts_ a member variable? It’s used only in integrate and would be better
left as an argument to that method.

Line 45 - 47: N, M, and S need to be doc’d.

Line 177: Split this up into two if/then and move the common code in between, as in


if (solver == 0)
cvode_mem_ = CVodeCreate(CV_ADAMS, CV_FUNCTIONAL);
else
cvode_mem_ = CVodeCreate(CV_BDF, CV_NEWTON);

if (cvode_mem_ == NULL)
throw std::runtime_error("CVodeCreate failed to allocate memory”);

set_cvode_options(rel_tol, abs_tol, max_num_steps);

if (solver != 0) {
// for the stiff solvers we need to reserve additional
// memory and provide a Jacobian function call
check_flag(CVDense(cvode_mem_, N_), "CVDense");
check_flag(CVDlsSetDenseJacFn(cvode_mem_, &solver::dense_jacobian),
"CVDlsSetDenseJacFn");
}

if (solver == 2)
check_flag(CVodeSetStabLimDet(cvode_mem_, 1), "CVodeSetStabLimDet”);

Note sure if "set_cvode_options(rel_tol, abs_tol, max_num_steps);” needs to be
factored into its own function as it would be called only once, but not a big deal
either way.

Line 214: I don’t think you need the braces, but not critical to remove them.

Line 252: Why cast to a solver const pointer? Did you mean const solver?

Line 312+: Can’t all of these methods be moved into ode_system, and then
pass a pointer to the ode_system implementation in CVodeSetUserData?
I think that’s the more natural factoring here.

Hi!

Thanks for your comments. Let me answer inline…

> Am 08.05.2016 um 17:07 schrieb Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com>:
>
> Firstly, a reminder that moving forward we should use more descriptive branch names,
> at least not having mysterious numerical labels! Something like “refactor_integrate_ode”

> do so before a pull request.

Well, the CVODES stuff is getting a (long) history. I can rename, but then we loose the current pull request

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/283

And the comments there were good, I think. Let’s quickly touch base tomorrow if we want to start from scratch with a new name and a new pull.

>
> ode_system.hpp
>
> Line 14: No reason to have abbreviations in comments.
>
> Line 15: “S” and “P” aren’t used in this implementation, no need to define them.
>
> Line 21: If it’s got methods, it’s a class. Just style.
>
> Line 57, 76, etc: Qualitifers/types on same line. So “inline void” instead of “inline\nvoid”
Thanks. Some comments still described old design (the abbreviations); I adapted this and tried to follow those style rules as I assume these are standard in Stan.

>
> integrate_ode_bdf.hpp
>
> Line 32: No abbreviations. This is worth a few sentences.
>
> Line 87: I recommend breaking this line to
>
>
> cvodes_integrator<F, T_initial, T_param>
> integrator(f, y0, t0,…
>
> to free up lots of vertical space.
Ok, done.

>
> cvodes_integrator.hpp
>
> Line 44: Why is ts_ a member variable? It’s used only in integrate and would be better
> left as an argument to that method.

I would prefer to leave it where it is. It belongs together with y0 and t0, I think. Moreover, we may want to revisit at some point the initial step size of cvode - it sets the initial step size based an a scary guess of y’’ and it is nowhere documented how this is done. So maybe we would like to set the initial step-size when configuring cvode in the constructor based on a scan through ts at some point.

>
> Line 45 - 47: N, M, and S need to be doc’d.
>
Sure. I add some notes for other bookkeeping ints as well.

> Line 177: Split this up into two if/then and move the common code in between, as in
>
>
> if (solver == 0)
> cvode_mem_ = CVodeCreate(CV_ADAMS, CV_FUNCTIONAL);
> else
> cvode_mem_ = CVodeCreate(CV_BDF, CV_NEWTON);
>
> if (cvode_mem_ == NULL)
> throw std::runtime_error("CVodeCreate failed to allocate memory”);
>
> set_cvode_options(rel_tol, abs_tol, max_num_steps);
>
> if (solver != 0) {
> // for the stiff solvers we need to reserve additional
> // memory and provide a Jacobian function call
> check_flag(CVDense(cvode_mem_, N_), "CVDense");
> check_flag(CVDlsSetDenseJacFn(cvode_mem_, &solver::dense_jacobian),
> "CVDlsSetDenseJacFn");
> }
>
> if (solver == 2)
> check_flag(CVodeSetStabLimDet(cvode_mem_, 1), "CVodeSetStabLimDet”);
>
> Note sure if "set_cvode_options(rel_tol, abs_tol, max_num_steps);” needs to be
> factored into its own function as it would be called only once, but not a big deal
> either way.
>

Your proposal is very close to what I had before. Daniel and Bob found it to be preferable to have a single if/then/else - as such a set_cvode_option function makes a lot of sense. I am leaving it for the moment as is, since this way of writing was seen as a step forward.
> Line 214: I don’t think you need the braces, but not critical to remove them.
Yes, they are not needed, but actually I prefer them to write them one time too often rather than forgetting.

>
> Line 252: Why cast to a solver const pointer? Did you mean const solver?
const applies to what is on the left as I learned recently (and only to the right if nothing is left of it); I changed to const solver if that is more natural to read.

>
> Line 312+: Can’t all of these methods be moved into ode_system, and then
> pass a pointer to the ode_system implementation in CVodeSetUserData?
> I think that’s the more natural factoring here.

The intent of the design is to keep all C related code inside cvodes_integrator such that we have a single point where this interface to the C library happens. Moreover, having ode_system like it is now will allow us to (i) refactor the coupled_ode_system object using ode_system and (ii) have a straightforward way to supply analytic Jacobians to our ODE solvers using partial template specialization. I hope this makes sense to you, I believe Bob and Daniel came to agree to this approach.

In the meantime I added tests for the decouple_ode_states and the ode_system object. I hope those tests are inline with the overall testing strategy.

Thanks again for looking.

Best,
Sebastian

I would think all of those would be arguments. I prefer to have

to reason about. For instance, if you ever change any of y0, t0
or ts, you have to enforce consistency (t0 < ts[n]).

> Moreover, we may want to revisit at some point the initial step size of cvode - it sets the initial step size based an a scary guess of y’’ and it is nowhere documented how this is done. So maybe we would like to set the initial step-size when configuring cvode in the constructor based on a scan through ts at some point.
Should we leave the initial step size in as a parameter?

>> pass a pointer to the ode_system implementation in CVodeSetUserData?
>> I think that’s the more natural factoring here.

I hope this makes sense to you, I believe Bob and Daniel came to agree to this approach.

Yes, fine by me. I like the encapsulation.

I have a very strong preference to use references rather than
pointers wherever possible. But I understand the external interface
requires pointers in some cases.

Thanks for looking into all this. I'm sure if we had a couple
more programmers, you could get two more different opinions :-)

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] cvodes_integrator feedback?
parts:
Hi!

Sounds like we are converging as opinions (other than mine) start to even revert code.

Concerning the step_size: I don't think we should expose it as the automatic defaults appear to work very good in all instances I have seen so far. The rationale Michael noted to not expose stuff which gets adapted is a good one from my perspective.

Wrt to the ts vector: You argumentation supports the current design, right? I mean the t0, y0 and ts are stored inside cvodes_integrator in const references.

To your last point about pointers: They cannot be totally avoided in this context, but I did try to avoid them as much as possible.

As now opinions start to diverge - is there a process in place to decide when things are final/ready to be merged?

Sebastian
